claude.sample_unit: patients (test set; 547 total, read by 6 radiologists)

links.outcome: Radiologist diagnostic performance with vs without AI assistance (independent vs second vs concurrent reading)
links.effect: Experienced AUC 0.83 to 0.90 (P<0.001); novice AUC 0.68 to 0.84 (second) and 0.85 (concurrent), P<0.001; specificity in novices 57.4% to 82.7%/83.3%.
links.quote: Similarly, novice radiologists also showed significantly improved AUC (second-reading: 0.84 vs. 0.68, P<0.001; concurrent-reading: 0.85 vs. 0.68, P<0.001), sensitivity (second-reading: 87.5% vs. 79.2%, P<0.001; concurrent-reading: 88.1% vs. 79.2%, P<0.001), and specificity (second-reading: 82.7% vs. 57.4%, P<0.001; concurrent-reading: 83.3% vs. 57.4%, P<0.001) compared with independent-reading.

links.outcome: Clinician performance with AI in intended reading workflow vs standalone model
links.effect: Experienced radiologists with AI outperformed DL-3DABUV alone (AUC 0.90 vs 0.82); novices reached parity with the AI (0.84-0.85 vs 0.82).
links.quote: Experienced radiologists achieved significantly better diagnostic performance in both second-reading and concurrent-reading modes compared with DL-3DABUV alone (all P<0.01 for AUC, sensitivity, and specificity; Table 1 and Supplementary Table 1 ).

links.outcome: AI diagnostic performance compared with experienced and novice radiologists on same data
links.effect: AI vs experienced: AUC 0.82 vs 0.83 (P=0.230); vs novice: AUC 0.82 vs 0.68 (P<0.001), specificity 81.5% vs 57.4% (P<0.001).
links.quote: Compared with novice radiologists in independent-reading mode, DL-3DABUV showed significantly higher AUC (0.82 vs. 0.68, P<0.001) and specificity (81.5% vs. 57.4%, P<0.001), while maintaining comparable sensitivity (82.1% vs. 79.2%, P=0.590).

links.outcome: Diagnostic performance and reading time by AI presentation timing (second vs concurrent reading)
links.effect: No significant differences in diagnostic performance between second and concurrent reading (e.g., experienced AUC 0.90 vs 0.90, P=0.500); concurrent reading saved 33.6 s per case (P<0.001).
links.quote: However, there were no significant differences between second-reading and concurrent-reading in AUC (experienced radiologists: 0.90 vs. 0.90, P=0.500; novice radiologists: 0.84 vs. 0.85, P>0.99), sensitivity (experienced radiologists: 90.5% vs. 91.7%, P>0.99; novice radiologists: 87.5% vs. 88.1%, P>0.99), or specificity (experienced radiologists: 92.0% vs. 92.0%, P=0.156; novice radiologists: 82.7% vs. 83.3%, P=0.157).

links.outcome: Test-set leakage and single-center generalizability of model development
links.effect: Model parameters were optimized using the test set; single-center retrospective random split without external validation.
links.quote: Network training was performed on the training set, with parameters optimized using the test set.

unlisted_practices: Comparing second-reading versus concurrent-reading AI workflow for reading time efficiency
Direct video-level deep learning without manual annotation
Using AI to assist novice radiologists to reduce unnecessary biopsies

openai.sample_unit: patients; 110 test patients evaluated by 6 radiologists

links.effect: AUC 0.82 vs experienced 0.83 (P=0.230); sensitivity 82.1% vs 81.6%; specificity 81.5% vs 88.3%.
links.quote: As shown in Table 1 and Supplementary Table 1 , DL-3DABUV demonstrated diagnostic performance comparable to that of experienced radiologists in independent-reading mode, with no significant differences in AUC (0.82 vs. 0.83, P=0.230), sensitivity (82.1% vs. 81.6%, P>0.99), or specificity (81.5% vs. 88.3%, P=0.126).

links.outcome: Radiologist performance with versus without AI
links.effect: Experienced AUC: 0.90 in both assisted modes vs 0.83 independent; novice AUC: 0.84/0.85 vs 0.68, all P<0.001.
links.quote: According to Table 1 and Supplementary Table 1 , both second-reading and concurrent-reading modes significantly improved diagnostic performance compared with independent-reading for both experienced and novice radiologists.

links.outcome: Reading time by AI reading mode
links.effect: Concurrent reading reduced mean time by 13.5 seconds vs independent and 33.6 seconds vs second-reading; both P<0.001.
links.quote: Compared with both independent-reading and second-reading, concurrent-reading resulted in significantly shorter reading times for all radiologists, with mean differences of 13.5 seconds (95% confidence interval [CI], 12.7 to 14.2; P<0.001) and 33.6 seconds (95% CI, 32.5 to 34.6; P<0.001), respectively ( Table 3 ).

links.outcome: Diagnostic performance of human-AI integration vs standalone AI
links.effect: Experienced radiologists assisted by DL-3DABUV achieved significantly higher AUC (0.90 vs 0.82), sensitivity (90.5%-91.7% vs 82.1%), and specificity (92.0% vs 81.5%) than DL-3DABUV alone (all P<0.01).
links.quote: Experienced radiologists achieved significantly better diagnostic performance in both second-reading and concurrent-reading modes compared with DL-3DABUV alone (all P<0.01 for AUC, sensitivity, and specificity; Table 1 and Supplementary Table 1 ).
